notes: Opens in mid-sentence ("Y en el párrafo siguiente..."). Checking the raw file data/raw/senado/taquigraficas/1998-06-03_r22_ORDINARIA.html before offset 178952 confirms this is the tail of senator Berhongaray's turn proposing two amendments, so it is not listed as a start. TWO PLACES where the page reprints a bold label for the SAME speaker immediately after a stenographer's note, with nobody else speaking in between: (a) "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" / "Reitero: está muy claro que la aprobación del artículo 1" after the note "-Varios señores senadores hablan a la vez."; (b) "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" / "Queda definitivamente sancionado el proyecto de ley." after the three voting notes. I first read rule 2 as making each of these a continuation of the turn already in progress and emitted 18 starts. The question was settled against that reading on the project's own evidence — the corpus convention recorded in TODO.md, the PDF gold set (gold_2004-04-28_p24.json lists four separate "Sr. Presidente. —" starts across two electronic votes), and the parser giving 497 distinct turn_ids to 497 labelled rows in one sitting: a printed label ALWAYS opens a turn, and rule 2 covers only an UNLABELLED continuation paragraph, speech that runs on with no label of its own. Both (a) and (b) are therefore listed in place and THE COUNT IS SETTLED AT 20 under the printed-label convention. Label punctuation varies between "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" and "Sr. PRESIDENTE.- " (a trailing space inside the bold run); I recorded the printed characters only and dropped that trailing space, since it is whitespace and not part of the terminator. The presiding officer is never named in this fragment, so the label stays the bare "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-". No inserted documents, headings or furniture in this stretch; the quoted statutory text inside the president's turn ("Sustitúyese el artículo 29...", "Apruébase como Régimen Simplicado...") is him reading aloud from the bill while speaking, not an insertion, so it stays inside his turn. "Simplicado" is the typist's misspelling of "Simplificado", left as printed. Markup trap: the fragment holds 21 bold runs but only 20 are labels — inside the president's turn "Señor senador Berhongaray: yo hice votar en general..." there is a stray empty bold run, "artículo 1° y dije", which is a WordPerfect artefact and not a speaker label. All 20 real labels are listed, one start each.
